title: API Token Retirement, Escrow & Scope Assertion Playbook
creator: Priya Natarajan
description:
Problem: Current token lifecycle is inconsistent across hosted/Dedicated/Private. We lack a single playbook for: emergency revocation, escrowed rotation, deterministic naming, and cryptographic scope assertions that tie tokens to RBAC v2 principals. This causes delayed responses to incidents and makes forensic audit trails noisy.

Goal: Produce an operational playbook and implement infra pieces to enable: (1) automated rotation with escrow and phased retirement, (2) per-scope token issuance (least privilege by default), (3) deterministic, searchable naming conventions, (4) instant cross-region revocation propagation, and (5) explicit audit links between token events and SSO/SAML/Identity assertions.

Scope: Hosted API tokens, service-account tokens, per-scope scoped keys (read/write/embed), admin tokens used by Console and internal services. Not in scope: customer-managed HSM key material lifecycle (handled in separate customer-onprem project).
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc in Confluence (link in attachments) with step-by-step emergency revocation runbook and post-incident checklist.
API + Console surfaces to request rotation and show escrow status for tokens (UI and API).
Deterministic naming applied to newly minted tokens and retrofitted for active tokens via migration job with idempotent semantics.
Revocation propagation observed under 30s SLO across regions for tokens revoked via admin console or programmatic API.
Audit events emitted for every lifecycle change with identity assertion (SSO/SAML session id, subject, auth_time) attached.
E2E test coverage for rotation, forced-revoke, and audit linkage in CI with synthetic identity assertions.
tasks: Design: finalize token naming schema and per-scope claim format (security + product review).
Infra: implement escrow store (encrypted) and rotation scheduler with safe-rollback windows.
Auth: add scope-assertion JWT payload fields and signers mapping to RBAC v2 principal IDs.
Console: UX for token retirement, escrow view, and forced revoke with warnings and trace id.
Migration: backfill existing token metadata and add 'retirement_epoch' field; ensure idempotent run.
Observability: add audit log schema changes, create dashboard for revoked tokens, and alert on abnormal revoke spikes.
Runbook: write emergency revocation playbook and run a tabletop exercise with SRE & SOC.
decisions: Adopt a 90-day default expiry for non-service tokens, 365 for long-lived service tokens with mandatory escrow.
Escrow store will be KMS-backed envelope encryption (AWS KMS + customer-managed KMS optional for Private).
Per-scope tokens will carry a 'scopes' claim and an immutable 'bound_principal_id' claim linked to RBAC v2 subject ID.
Revocation propagation will use a pub/sub fanout to sidecars and region control planes; best-effort immediate deny + eventual consistency safeguards.

2025-10-01 - Alex Chen (SRE): Load test notes: revocation fanout handled 10k keys/second across regions in staging; need to tune backpressure to avoid control-plane overload.

migration_plan: Phase 1: Read-only metadata backfill (2-day job) to attach binding_principal_id and compute deterministic names. Phase 2: Enable new issuance flows and mark old tokens as legacy. Phase 3: Scheduled rotation windows for legacy tokens, with opt-out for critical service tokens after manual review.
rollout_plan: Beta rollout to internal teams (Console + API) -> Dedicated customers opt-in -> Private release with config flags. Monitor revocation latency and audit integrity; hold release if >1% of revocations exceed 60s propagation.
test_plan: Unit tests for claim generation; integration tests for escrow encryption+decryption; chaos test for control-plane outage during revocation; tabletop emergency exercise.
failure_modes: Escrow KMS key compromise -> rotate KMS keys and force re-emit tokens; Revocation queue backpressure -> degrade to region-only deny until control plane recovers; Missing identity assertions -> reject admin rotations (require re-auth).
notes: This ticket ties closely to RBAC v2 schema changes; coordinate with PM to avoid principal ID churn during rollout. Ensure compliance team signs off on retention/escrow durations.
